Your AI vendor might know more about your business than your board does.

Enterprise AI spending is projected to hit $37.5 billion in 2026, according to Gartner — up from near zero just four years ago. But here is the part most executive teams have not fully reckoned with: every time your organization feeds proprietary data, workflows, and decisions into an external AI system, the provider potentially learns how your business operates.

Palantir just made a very public push for what they are calling 'AI sovereignty' — the idea that enterprises should be able to fine-tune and run models while keeping their data, memory, and model weights entirely under their own control. This is not a niche technical concern. It is a boardroom-level strategic question.

The next phase of enterprise AI will not be defined by which model has the best benchmarks. It will be defined by who owns the intelligence accumulated through daily use. Companies that treat AI integration as a procurement decision will eventually discover their competitive advantage living on someone else's infrastructure. Companies that treat it as an ownership decision will compound that advantage over time.
